Branch coverage

Source: R/branches.R
covr.branch_coverage.Rd

By setting options(covr.branch_coverage = TRUE) before measuring coverage, covr also records which branches of each if and switch() in R code were taken. Line and expression coverage are the same as without it. Branch coverage is experimental: what counts as a branch, and how branches are stored and reported, may change.

Details

The option is read when the code is instrumented, so it has no cost when it is not set. When it is set, every if and switch() that runs calls a function of covr, which makes the code slower.

Branches

  • An if has two branches, "TRUE" and "FALSE". The "FALSE" branch of an if without an else is taken when the condition is FALSE. Nothing is recorded if the condition is NA or otherwise signals an error.

  • A switch() has a branch for each of its arms, labelled with the name of the arm. Arms that fall through to the next arm (switch(x, a = , b = 1)) share its branch, labelled "a, b". An unnamed arm is labelled "<default>", or with its position if all arms are unnamed. A switch() without a default arm has another branch, "<no match>", taken when no arm matches, including a number that selects no arm. A switch() with arms in ... has no branches.

&&, || and loops have no branches, nor does compiled code.

If the line where an if or switch() starts is excluded, e.g. with # nocov (see exclusions), all its branches are excluded too.

Results

The branches are in the branches attribute of the coverage object, a list with an element for each if and switch(), named like the elements of the coverage object (see coverage). Each is a list with the srcref of the if or switch(), its functions, the labels of its branches, and value, the number of times each branch was taken. Use tally_coverage(by = "branch") for a data frame with one row for each branch, and percent_coverage(by = "branch") for the percentage of branches taken.

to_lcov(), to_cobertura(), codecov() and coveralls() include the branches. Codecov shows a line with branches that weren't all taken as partly covered, and counts it as not covered in the coverage percentage, so the percentage on Codecov is lower with branch coverage. report(), file_report() and to_sonarqube() don't include the branches yet.

Examples

withr::with_options(list(covr.branch_coverage = TRUE), {
  cov <- code_coverage(
    "f <- function(x) {\n  if (x > 0) 'positive'\n  'done'\n}",
    "f(1)"
  )
})
tally_coverage(cov, by = "branch")
#>                               filename functions line column branch label value
#> 1 /tmp/Rtmp997BL9/source.R1857339b77db         f    2      3      1  TRUE     1
#> 2 /tmp/Rtmp997BL9/source.R1857339b77db         f    2      3      2 FALSE     0
percent_coverage(cov, by = "branch")
#> [1] 50
